transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-11 | 14:00 - 14:56 UTC | Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Ava Li (Redwood Product), Liam O'Rourke (NimbusSphere CTO), Sana Malik (NimbusSphere Partnerships), Diego Ramos (NimbusSphere Platform Eng), Maya Patel (NimbusSphere Security)

Summary (auto): align on marketplace integration, reference architecture, security checklist, pilot timeline.

[00:00:00] Jordan Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on partners. priya and ava from our side.
[00:00:12] Liam O'Rourke: hey Jordan, thanks. Liam here. excited to dig in, we've been looking at the marketplace flow and the reference arch you sent.
[00:00:25] Priya Kapoor: great, i'll run through the integration points, high level reference arch, and then we'll talk pages - marketplace checklist and security.
[00:00:40] Sana Malik: perfect. our main goals are: 1) get listed on AWS/GCP marketplace, 2) have a validated deployment option for customers through Redwood, and 3) co-marketing. timeline is q4 pilot ideally.
[00:01:05] Priya Kapoor: makes sense. first, listing: there's the listing package - images, pricing matrix, billing integration. Jordan will share the exact checklist but important bits are: marketplace listing doc, x86/arm builder images (if applicable), and a listing SKU that maps to Redwood's billing for hosted/dedicated.
[00:01:28] Diego Ramos: quick q - when you say map to Redwood billing, do you mean we bill through Redwood and get settled, or we keep billing and just list a connector?
[00:01:39] Jordan Chen: good q. we support both patterns. for AWS Marketplace there's a SaaS subscription or private offers flow. typically for joint solutions we recommend routing usage through Redwood's billing if you want unified invoicing and a smoother customer experience; we can also do connector-only where Nimbus keeps billing. that'll change contract terms and revenue share.
[00:02:05] Maya Patel: from security: we need to confirm what data persists in Redwood's logs and what remains in our VPC. Does Redwood support private deployments with a customer-managed control plane?
[00:02:18] Priya Kapoor: yes - Redwood Private (you may see it as Redwood Private or Redwood VPC) supports a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options. KV cache and model artifacts can be configured to not leave your VPC. note - transcription: sometimes docs say KV cash in earlier notes, that's a typo.
[00:02:37] Diego Ramos: ha, KV cash. ok. for the pilot we'd prefer a dedicated footprint in Redwood Dedicated or a private deployment in our own VPC. concerns are latency and compliance.
[00:02:50] Ava Li: for latency/dedicated: we can provision Dedicated pools pinned to your tenant - predictable throughput and SLOs. tradeoffs are cost vs latency; we can recommend batching/quant profiles to reduce token costs.
[00:03:10] Liam O'Rourke: can you share what the expected unit economics look like? i.e., costs for reserved capacity vs hosted consumption?
[00:03:19] Jordan Chen: i'll share a pricing matrix. rough rule: dedicated reserved capacity is better at sustained high throughput > X tokens/sec; hosted pay-as-you-go is better for spiky workloads. we'll include sample numbers in the checklist.
[00:03:38] Priya Kapoor: moving to reference architecture - slide 1: customer traffic to Nimbus UI -> Redwood API -> model runtime. for private deployments the flow is customer -> your VPC -> Redwood control plane (optional) -> runtime. make sure you pin model versions for rollouts.
[00:04:05] Sana Malik: what about SSO and RBAC? we need SAML for our enterprise customers.
[00:04:12] Priya Kapoor: Redwood Console supports SSO/SAML and RBAC; we integrate with common IdPs. we'll document the attribute mappings.
[00:04:26] Maya Patel: encryption at rest? KMS/HSM support?
[00:04:30] Priya Kapoor: yes - customer-managed KMS for private deployments; we also support HSM integration for key storage. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. sometimes our docs refer to 'Redwood Consol' with a misspelling, ignore that.
[00:04:47] Diego Ramos: great. On terraform - do you have modules we can reuse for provisioning?
[00:04:52] Priya Kapoor: yes, we have sample terraform modules for provisioning Dedicated pools and VPC connectors. i'll attach an example repo link.
[00:05:10] Jordan Chen: i also want to call out testing and acceptance criteria for the marketplace listing: a staging deployment with end-to-end flow, security checklist signed off, and sample performance benchmarks under target latency.
[00:05:27] Liam O'Rourke: benchmarks - can you run a small trial to show tail latency for 4k tokens? our use case tends to have longer contexts.
[00:05:36] Priya Kapoor: we can. we'll propose a micro-benchmark plan in the repo. note that quantization and kernel selection can change latency tradeoffs; we'll document recommended configs.
[00:05:55] Sana Malik: about joint materials - we'd like a reference architecture whitepaper and a co-branded marketplace blurb. timeline?
[00:06:03] Jordan Chen: if we start pilot week of 9/22 we can aim for a marketplace listing in late october, co-marketing in parallel. needs approvals from legal for revenue share.
[00:06:20] Maya Patel: legal will want to see SOC2 and ISO attestations. can you provide SOC2 Type II report and any penetration test summaries?
[00:06:29] Priya Kapoor: yes - i can share our SOC2 artifacts and a security packet. we'll redact sensitive bits but include attestations and scope.
[00:06:45] Diego Ramos: small nit - in your earlier docs some product names got swapped, like Redwood Optimize vs Redwood Dedicated. can you confirm which features are in each product?
[00:06:55] Ava Li: sure - Redwood Dedicated = reserved GPU pools and capacity; Redwood Optimize is tooling for batching/quant/observability. we'll include a matrix.
[00:07:12] [07:12 elapsed in meeting, transcript jumps forward] Jordan Chen: ok let's talk integration steps - 1) marketplace assets and legal terms, 2) staging deployment + test harness, 3) security/compliance sign-off, 4) pilot and metrics, 5) listing and go-live.
[00:07:31] Priya Kapoor: technical details - for billing integration we support metering via tokens or a subscription SKU. if Nimbus wants to surface Redwood-hosted models under your listing, we can expose SKUs that map to usage.
[00:07:48] Liam O'Rourke: will that require customers to have Redwood accounts?
[00:07:52] Jordan Chen: depends. for unified billing, customer can sign up through the marketplace flow and be represented in Redwood's account model; we can also add SSO and map external IDs.
[00:08:05] Diego Ramos: on logging - we need to ensure PII isn't persisted. is there a redact option?
[00:08:12] Priya Kapoor: yes, we offer request/response redaction rules and PII scrubbing at the proxy layer. that's configurable per-tenant.
[00:08:26] Sana Malik: ok good. next, can we run through the pilot acceptance criteria quickly?
[00:08:30] Jordan Chen: sure - acceptance criteria draft: (a) staging deployment operational with sample traffic, (b) latency within 95th percentile target (we'll define numbers), (c) security docs signed off, (d) listing assets ready, (e) joint marketing brief approved.
[00:08:55] Priya Kapoor: i'll put together the acceptance test plan and the sample load script (we've used locust/gatling in the past).
[00:09:08] Liam O'Rourke: ok timeline sounds good. any blockers from Redwood side?
[00:09:13] Jordan Chen: none from infra, but legal needs to finalize marketplace revenue terms. we'll loop in our commercial team after this sync.
[00:09:25] Maya Patel: security question - if we go with Redwood Dedicated, who holds keys for model artifacts?
[00:09:30] Priya Kapoor: Dedicated is still managed by Redwood but isolated pools; for full control you should choose Private deployment where you manage KMS. Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed KMS in many cases but there are some provider limitations. we'll enumerate them.
[00:09:54] Diego Ramos: curious about fallback - if a region is unavailable can traffic failover to Redwood-hosted fallback model with lower cost?
[00:10:02] Ava Li: yes - smart routing can fall back to compatible model variants in a different region or lower-capacity tier. config is in the routing policy.
[00:10:18] [10:18 elapsed] Jordan Chen: ok let's capture concrete items: Jordan will send the checklist, priya will share the arch and terraform, diego will grant staging. any other asks?
[00:10:30] Sana Malik: can you also provide a sample marketplace listing blurb and logo requirements?
[00:10:35] Jordan Chen: yes. we'll include image dimensions, descriptions, and sample copy.
[00:10:45] Liam O'Rourke: for the pilot, we want a demo run with a 4k token context with embeddings + rerank. can you support that?
[00:10:55] Priya Kapoor: yes that's within scope. we'll include that in the benchmark plan.
[00:11:12] [11:12 elapsed, meeting moves into Q&A and smaller clarifications across the next ~40 minutes, transcript highlights below]
[00:12:00] Priya Kapoor: linking to repo: github.com/redwood/integrations/nimbussphere (note: placeholder link, actual link will be shared)
[00:15:22] Diego Ramos: terraform module question - does it create the dedicated pool and a VPC connector?
[00:15:28] Priya Kapoor: yes, example does both; it's idempotent and has variables for region and machine types.
[00:20:05] Maya Patel: on compliance, our audit requires logs to be retained 1 year and also be exportable to our SIEM. can Redwood support custom retention?
[00:20:18] Priya Kapoor: yes, log retention and export are configurable. longer retention is an add-on in some plans.
[00:25:40] Jordan Chen: competitors - ModelServeCo and CloudAI Endpoints mentioned as comparison; Redwood differentiators are the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private and the tooling for cost/perf tradeoffs.
[00:31:10] Priya Kapoor: small transcription note - we sometimes say 'Redwood Optimize' for cost tooling and 'Redwood Console' for observability; you'll get a short product mapping doc.
[00:38:00] Diego Ramos: what about E2E tests - can Redwood run them against our staging account and report metrics?
[00:38:10] Priya Kapoor: yes, we can run benchmark jobs and push results to the repo. we'll include sample dashboards.
[00:44:05] Sana Malik: co-marketing - we have 3 assets in mind: a BRD-style reference architecture whitepaper, a joint blog announcement, and a webinar. we need to confirm timeline for copy and approvals.
[00:44:22] Jordan Chen: we'll draft a timeline in the next deck.
[00:50:00] Maya Patel: last security question - penetration test: do you allow us to run an external pentest for the integration?
[00:50:08] Priya Kapoor: yes, we have a pentest process and coordination window; we'll share the program.
[00:51:30] Jordan Chen: great, let's recap next steps and owners.
[00:51:45] [Recap] Jordan Chen: 1) Jordan send marketplace checklist and sample pricing by 9/14. 2) Priya send reference arch + terraform by 9/18. 3) Diego provide staging access and sample model by 9/21. 4) Maya share compliance requirements by 9/20. 5) Sana confirm co-marketing budget by 9/25.
[00:52:05] Liam O'Rourke: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[00:52:12] Jordan Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with links and invite for pilot kickoff.
[00:52:20] Meeting end
